headline: Broad-based demand strength lifts margins across the board
summary_short: MACOM's fiscal Q1 2026 revenue rose to $289.0M, up 22.5% y/y (6.4% q/q), as gross margin expanded to 56.9% and operating income climbed 45.8% y/y to $50.8M; diluted EPS of $0.60 was up 42.9% y/y but down 6.3% q/q on a normalizing tax rate.
summary_long: Revenue grew 22.5% y/y to $289.0M, led by Data Center (+36.0% y/y, higher-speed optical/analog sales), I&D (+22.4% y/y, defense programs) and Telecom (+7.6% y/y, PON/SATCOM demand). Gross margin expanded to 56.9% from 55.2% y/y on pricing and volume leverage, partly offset by added RTP Fab headcount. Operating income rose 45.8% y/y to $50.8M as gross-profit growth outpaced R&D/SG&A increases. Net income of $46.3M (diluted EPS $0.60) rose y/y but fell q/q on a higher effective tax rate versus an unusually low prior quarter. MACOM fully repaid its $161.2M 2026 Convertible Notes, cutting short-term debt to zero; cash fell to $98.5M. No forward guidance was disclosed in this filing.

drivers.explanation: Broad-based growth: I&D revenue +22.4% y/y on defense program strength, Data Center +36.0% y/y on higher sales of analog, coherent and optical products for 100G-1.6T interconnects, and Telecom +7.6% y/y on PON, metro, broadband access and SATCOM demand.

Margin rose to 56.9% from 55.2% y/y as higher sales more than offset increased employee-related costs from added RTP Fab headcount, higher maintenance expense and greater production-supplies spending.

Growth reflects gross profit expanding faster (+26.3% y/y) than combined opex: R&D +19.3% q/q and SG&A +19.1% q/q, both driven by higher headcount, share-based compensation and professional/software costs per the filing.

Net income dipped q/q despite higher operating income because the effective tax rate normalized to 18.6% this quarter from an unusually low prior-quarter rate; y/y growth (+46.3%) tracks the underlying operating improvement.
Cash fell q/q and y/y as $121.6M of six-month operating cash flow was more than offset by $161.2M used to repay the 2026 Convertible Notes, $51.5M of employee-tax stock withholding, and capex.
The current portion of long-term debt fell to zero after MACOM repaid the full $161.2 million outstanding balance of its 2026 Convertible Notes during the six months ended April 3, 2026.
